active_problem.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).
A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) used ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED (E-03).
Field route completion for manual-read accounts fell to 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026 (E-02).
Dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) despite the surge (E-01).
active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1180→1260 monthly, E-07), driven primarily by the "billing import + validation" step of meter-to-cash issuing incorrect bills from accepted ACTUAL meter reads rather than by slow dispute handling (E-01, within SLA) or missing reads (majority of disputed bills, 1785/3025, are ACTUAL-type, not ESTIMATED, E-03). The best-supported mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is a change to billing import validation rules around August that misclassifies or mis-rates valid accepted reads into wrong bills, producing the dispute surge.

VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (billing-config) actually show a rule change around August that would misclassify or mis-rate accepted ACTUAL reads?

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data shows median dispute response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets. This indicates response-handling speed is not breaching SLA despite the surge, undercutting the claim that slow ticket handling is driving the doubled dispute volume.

Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 accounts. This shortfall means a material block of manual reads were not completed as scheduled, which is a plausible driver of increased estimate substitution and wrong bills for those accounts.

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (3025 total): a majority of disputed bills were generated from an accepted actual meter read, not an estimate. This undercuts estimate-substitution-centric causes (missing/late AMI or field reads) as the dominant driver and points toward something wrong in how accepted reads are turned into bills.

billing-db's tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff/rate changes were logged in the period under review, ruling out a tariff change as a cause of the wrong bills behind the dispute surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three readers since July is causing routes to run late, which in turn pushes those accounts to estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not confirmed data. symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).

active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07), coincident with validation rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13). BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw AMI register readings directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13); AMI firmware v4.2, rolled out 2026-06, reports register readings in 0.1 m3 units versus older firmware's whole m3 units (E-14), so BV-17 misreads normal v4.2 consumption as a ~10x spike. This causes billing import validation to reject valid, on-time AMI reads as "high consumption" and substitute an estimate instead: 1184 of the 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts show exactly this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern tagged firmware v4.2 (E-12). The resulting wrong estimated bills drive at least this AMI-metered portion of the surge; response-handling speed is within SLA (E-01) and no tariff change occurred (E-04), ruling out those alternatives. The mechanism behind the larger ACTUAL-read-type dispute share (1785/3025, E-03) is not yet confirmed and is flagged as an open unknown.

problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1180→1260 monthly, E-07), driven primarily by the "billing import + validation" step of meter-to-cash issuing incorrect bills from accepted ACTUAL meter reads rather than by slow dispute handling (E-01, within SLA) or missing reads (majority of disputed bills, 1785/3025, are ACTUAL-type, not ESTIMATED, E-03). The best-supported mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is a change to billing import validation rules around August that misclassifies or mis-rates valid accepted reads into wrong bills, producing the dispute surge.

release_summary.summary: The Customer Service lead (SH-CS, claim CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix "whatever is causing the wrong bills," framing the doubled dispute volume (610→1180→1260/month, E-07) as a slow-response problem. That framing was tested and contradicted: dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-01), so H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP was rejected. Investigation of billing data found that an August billing-import validation rule, BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13), compares raw AMI meter-register values to a 12-month m3 history; AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out June, E-14) reports in 0.1 m3 units instead of the legacy m3, so BV-17 misreads normal usage as a ~10x spike. This explains 1184 of 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, E-12). This finding invalidated the earlier problem definition (PD-1@v1, which had centered on mis-rated ACTUAL reads) and triggered a dependency review (DR-1) invalidating prior assumptions, work items and the first solution design; the problem was redefined as PD-1@v2 under a CONDITIONAL_PASS DEFINE gate. The release ships two deliverables: confirmation of the BV-17 rule change (DA-RULES, E-13) and dispute-volume trend monitoring (DA-TICKET, E-07); no bill-write or route-push actions are included, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH authority constraints. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: deterministic checks (layer1) passed, but one semantic check failed and the DEFINE gate itself was only conditional, so the release proceeds with a documented set of known limitations rather than a clean pass, and no items were put on hold.
key_points: SH-CS's initial framing (CL-01) that slow ticket handling caused the surge was tested against E-01 (response times within SLA) and rejected; the actual mechanism found is a billing-import validation defect, not a response-speed issue.

Root cause for the AMI-metered ESTIMATED-read dispute subset: validation rule BV-17 (E-13, deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling) misreads firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register units (E-14) as a consumption spike, confirmed in 1184 of 1240 cases (E-12).

This finding (E-12) invalidated the prior problem definition PD-1@v1 and its dependent assumptions, hypotheses, work items and solution design (DR-1); the problem was redefined as PD-1@v2 with DEFINE gate result CONDITIONAL_PASS.

Released deliverables (SD-2 release scope / PLAN-2): BV-17 rule-change confirmation (DA-RULES, E-13) and dispute-volume trend monitoring (DA-TICKET, E-07) — both read-only diagnostics, no bill writes or route pushes, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: deterministic verification passed, but a semantic check (stated_limitations_vs_data_asset_records) failed and the DEFINE gate was only a conditional pass; no hold items were raised.

The dominant cause of the majority ACTUAL-read-type disputes (1785/3025, E-03) remains unconfirmed (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM OPEN) and is excluded from this release; no bill-correction proposal ships.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate for the current problem definition returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass; items deferred at that gate are tracked as open verification obligations rather than resolved before release.

A semantic consistency check failed: the stated unfinished-scope text and assumption A-RULE-LOG-COMPLETENESS describe DA-RULES and DA-TICKET completeness as UNKNOWN, but the data_assets records actually show both as COMPLETE — the stated rationale conflicts with the underlying record.

VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM is open and sits outside this release's scope: it is unconfirmed whether the BV-17/firmware mechanism, or something else, explains the larger ACTUAL-read-type dispute share (1785/3025, E-03).

Because that question is unresolved, the diagnostic queries into disputed-bill/AMI read detail and any draft bill-correction proposal are blocked; this release ships no fix or correction handoff for the ACTUAL-read disputes.
A vendor change request to the AMI provider (ORG-AMI/SH-AMI) to standardize or document firmware v4.2's register units has not been raised in this release.

Whether dispute volume will actually fall back to the pre-August ~600/month baseline once a fix is deployed is a stated expectation, not a confirmed outcome; the monthly figures so far (E-07) only show the surge, not recovery.

Completeness of the DA-RULES log (future unlogged rule changes could go undetected) and DA-TICKET sample is flagged as a limiting factor for monitoring precision, and whether Jun-Jul is a valid seasonal baseline (U-BASELINE-VALIDITY) remains an open question.

output.summary: The Customer Service lead (SH-CS, claim CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix "whatever is causing the wrong bills," framing the doubled dispute volume (610→1180→1260/month, E-07) as a slow-response problem. That framing was tested and contradicted: dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-01), so H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP was rejected. Investigation of billing data found that an August billing-import validation rule, BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13), compares raw AMI meter-register values to a 12-month m3 history; AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out June, E-14) reports in 0.1 m3 units instead of the legacy m3, so BV-17 misreads normal usage as a ~10x spike. This explains 1184 of 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, E-12). This finding invalidated the earlier problem definition (PD-1@v1, which had centered on mis-rated ACTUAL reads) and triggered a dependency review (DR-1) invalidating prior assumptions, work items and the first solution design; the problem was redefined as PD-1@v2 under a CONDITIONAL_PASS DEFINE gate. The release ships two deliverables: confirmation of the BV-17 rule change (DA-RULES, E-13) and dispute-volume trend monitoring (DA-TICKET, E-07); no bill-write or route-push actions are included, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH authority constraints. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: deterministic checks (layer1) passed, but one semantic check failed and the DEFINE gate itself was only conditional, so the release proceeds with a documented set of known limitations rather than a clean pass, and no items were put on hold.
key_points: SH-CS's initial framing (CL-01) that slow ticket handling caused the surge was tested against E-01 (response times within SLA) and rejected; the actual mechanism found is a billing-import validation defect, not a response-speed issue.

Root cause for the AMI-metered ESTIMATED-read dispute subset: validation rule BV-17 (E-13, deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling) misreads firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register units (E-14) as a consumption spike, confirmed in 1184 of 1240 cases (E-12).

This finding (E-12) invalidated the prior problem definition PD-1@v1 and its dependent assumptions, hypotheses, work items and solution design (DR-1); the problem was redefined as PD-1@v2 with DEFINE gate result CONDITIONAL_PASS.

Released deliverables (SD-2 release scope / PLAN-2): BV-17 rule-change confirmation (DA-RULES, E-13) and dispute-volume trend monitoring (DA-TICKET, E-07) — both read-only diagnostics, no bill writes or route pushes, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: deterministic verification passed, but a semantic check (stated_limitations_vs_data_asset_records) failed and the DEFINE gate was only a conditional pass; no hold items were raised.

The dominant cause of the majority ACTUAL-read-type disputes (1785/3025, E-03) remains unconfirmed (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM OPEN) and is excluded from this release; no bill-correction proposal ships.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate for the current problem definition returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass; items deferred at that gate are tracked as open verification obligations rather than resolved before release.

A semantic consistency check failed: the stated unfinished-scope text and assumption A-RULE-LOG-COMPLETENESS describe DA-RULES and DA-TICKET completeness as UNKNOWN, but the data_assets records actually show both as COMPLETE — the stated rationale conflicts with the underlying record.

VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM is open and sits outside this release's scope: it is unconfirmed whether the BV-17/firmware mechanism, or something else, explains the larger ACTUAL-read-type dispute share (1785/3025, E-03).

Because that question is unresolved, the diagnostic queries into disputed-bill/AMI read detail and any draft bill-correction proposal are blocked; this release ships no fix or correction handoff for the ACTUAL-read disputes.
A vendor change request to the AMI provider (ORG-AMI/SH-AMI) to standardize or document firmware v4.2's register units has not been raised in this release.

Whether dispute volume will actually fall back to the pre-August ~600/month baseline once a fix is deployed is a stated expectation, not a confirmed outcome; the monthly figures so far (E-07) only show the surge, not recovery.

Completeness of the DA-RULES log (future unlogged rule changes could go undetected) and DA-TICKET sample is flagged as a limiting factor for monitoring precision, and whether Jun-Jul is a valid seasonal baseline (U-BASELINE-VALIDITY) remains an open question.
